ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Don't Let Anger Be Your Boss

fullPassage:
Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life.

As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more intense than they really are. All of these factors can contribute to feelings of anger.

Getting to Know Your Anger

Anger is a natural emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated unfairly. The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a productive way so that it does not control you.

Questions to Ask Yourself

When you feel angry, it can be helpful to ask yourself some questions. Why am I feeling this way? Is my anger justified? Am I overreacting? What is the best way to handle this situation? Is there another way to look at this? What would I tell a friend in the same situation? These questions can help you step back and think more clearly before you act.

First Aid to Calm Yourself Down

When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists. These are signs that your body is preparing for a fight. But fighting is rarely the answer. Instead, try some first aid techniques to calm yourself down. Take deep breaths. Count to ten slowly. Walk away from the situation for a few minutes. Drink a glass of cold water. These simple actions can help bring your body back to a calm state.

Finding Proper Coping Skills

Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to deal with your anger. Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is problem-solving. Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.

Conclusion

Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a normal part of being human. But you have the power to choose how you respond to your anger. Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and finding proper coping skills, you can take control of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a healthier way.

questions.passage: Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life. As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become independent.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 청소년의 분노 감정은 단순히 일상 스트레스에서 비롯된다.
부모님은 청소년의 분노 감정을 항상 이해한다.
분노를 느끼는 것은 태도가 나쁘기 때문이다.

det.korean: 청소년기에 정체성을 발달시키고 독립적이 되려고 노력한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 원문 일치: You are developing your identity and trying to become independent.
❌ ① don't simply come from stress — 단순히 일상 스트레스에서만 오지 않음
❌ ② 부모님이 항상 이해한다는 언급 없음
❌ ④ 태도가 나쁘기 때문이라고 단정하지 않음(Some people may think)
det.tip: 원문은 '단순히 일상 스트레스에서만 오지 않는다'이지, '일상 스트레스에서 온다'가 아니다. don't simply에 주의!

questions.passage: Anger is a natural emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated unfairly. The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a productive way so that it does not control you.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 분노는 부당한 대우를 받을 때를 알려줄 수 있다.
분노를 생산적인 방식으로 관리하는 것이 핵심이다.

det.korean: 분노는 항상 나쁜 것은 아니다(not always a bad thing).
det.analysis:
✅ ① '항상 나쁜 것'이 아님. 원문: not always a bad thing(부분 부정)
❌ ② 원문 일치: tell you when you are being treated unfairly
❌ ③ 원문 일치: manage your anger in a productive way
❌ ④ 원문 일치: a natural emotion
det.tip: not always = 항상 ~은 아니다 (부분 부정). '항상 나쁘다'는 전체 긍정이므로 원문과 불일치.

questions.passage: When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists. These are signs that your body is preparing for a fight. But fighting is rarely the answer. Instead, try some __________ to calm yourself down.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 싸움 대신 진정시키기 위한 응급처치 기법(first aid techniques)을 시도하라.
det.analysis:
✅ ② first aid techniques: 원문 일치 — 깊은 호흡, 10까지 세기, 상황에서 벗어나기 등
❌ ① fighting strategies: 싸움 전략, 문맥 반대
❌ ③ medical treatments: 의료 치료, 과도
❌ ④ exercise routines: 운동 루틴, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: first aid(응급처치) — 분노 시 즉각적으로 진정하는 간단한 기법. 깊은 호흡, 10까지 세기 등.

questions.passage: Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is __________. Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 또 다른 유용한 기술은 문제 해결(problem-solving)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ problem-solving: 원문 일치 — 빈칸 뒤 'finding a solution to the problem'이 구체적 설명
❌ ① self-criticism: 자기 비판, 문맥 부적절
❌ ② denial: 부정, 건설적이지 않음
❌ ③ avoidance: 회피, 문맥 반대
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤의 'finding a solution to the problem'이 problem-solving의 구체적 설명이다.

questions.passage: As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more __________ than they really are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 호르몬이 감정을 실제보다 더 강렬하게(intense) 느끼게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① intense: 원문 일치 — 호르몬의 영향으로 감정이 실제보다 강하게 느껴짐
❌ ② stable: 안정적인, 문맥 반대
❌ ③ predictable: 예측 가능한, 문맥 부적절
❌ ④ manageable: 관리 가능한, 문맥 반대
det.tip: intense(강렬한) — 호르몬의 영향으로 감정이 실제보다 더 강하게 느껴진다는 맥락.

questions.passage: As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions __________ more intense than they really are.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형 구문. 호르몬이 감정을 더 강렬하게 '느끼게' 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① feel(동사원형): 사역동사 make + 목적어(your emotions) + 동사원형(feel)
❌ ② to feel: make는 to부정사를 취하지 않음
❌ ③ feeling: 현재분사, make 구문에 부적절
❌ ④ felt: 과거분사, make 구문에 부적절
det.tip: 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형: make는 원형부정사를 목적격 보어로 취한다. 수동태에서는 be made to do.

questions.passage: Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is problem-solving. Instead of __________ on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사가 와야 한다. instead of focusing on ~
det.analysis:
✅ ③ focusing(동명사): 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사(-ing)가 온다
❌ ① focus: 동사원형, 전치사 뒤 불가
❌ ② focused: 과거분사, 전치사 뒤 부적절
❌ ④ to focus: to부정사, 전치사 뒤 불가
det.tip: 전치사(of) + 동명사(-ing): instead of + 동명사. 전치사 뒤에는 명사/동명사만 가능.

questions.passage: The part of your brain __________ controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more intense than they really are.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주격 관계대명사 that. 선행사 the part를 수식하는 관계절의 주어 역할.
det.analysis:
✅ ② that: 주격 관계대명사 — the part(선행사) + that(주격) + controls(동사)
❌ ① who: 사람 선행사에만 사용
❌ ③ what: 선행사를 포함하므로 the part와 함께 사용 불가
❌ ④ where: 장소 관계부사, 주어 역할 불가
det.tip: 선행사(the part) + 관계대명사(that) + 동사(controls): 주격 관계대명사. which도 가능.

questions.passage: Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and __________ proper coping skills, you can take control of your emotions.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: By + 동명사 구문에서 and로 병렬 연결. understanding, asking, calming과 동일한 동명사 형태.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ finding(동명사): 병렬 구조 — By understanding, asking, calming, and finding
❌ ① find: 동사원형, 병렬 구조 불일치
❌ ② found: 과거형, 병렬 구조 불일치
❌ ③ to find: to부정사, 병렬 구조 불일치
det.tip: 병렬 구조: By understanding, asking, calming, and finding — 네 개의 동명사가 and로 연결.

questions.passage: As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. ( ① ) You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. ( ② ) At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. ( ③ ) The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. ( ④ ) All of these factors can contribute to feelings of anger.
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more intense than they really are."

det.korean: '게다가(On top of that)' 호르몬이 감정을 더 강렬하게 느끼게 한다. 뇌 발달 + 감정 영역 활발에 추가.
det.analysis:
✅ ④: On top of that(게다가)는 앞 내용에 추가. 뇌 미발달 + 감정 영역 활발에 호르몬 요인을 더함. All of these factors에 호르몬도 포함.
❌ ①②③: 호르몬 언급은 뇌 발달과 감정 영역 설명 이후에 나와야 자연스럽다.
det.tip: On top of that = 게다가, 그 위에. 앞의 요인들(뇌 미발달, 감정 영역 활발)에 호르몬을 추가로 언급.

questions.passage: Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to deal with your anger. ( ① ) Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. ( ② ) Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. ( ③ ) Another useful skill is problem-solving. ( ④ ) Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful."

det.korean: 신뢰하는 사람에게 이야기하는 것도 매우 도움이 된다. 대처법 나열 순서의 세 번째.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: 대처법 나열 — 산책/운동 → 그림/글쓰기 → 신뢰하는 사람과 대화(also 추가) → 문제해결(Another skill)
❌ ①: 방법 나열 시작 전
❌ ②: 첫 번째 방법과 두 번째 방법 사이
❌ ④: problem-solving 설명이 이어지는 위치
det.tip: also(또한)는 앞의 방법들에 추가. Another(③ 뒤)는 새 스킬 전환. 대화 → 문제해결 순서.

questions.passage:
When anger hits, your body reacts physically.

(A) These are signs that your body is preparing for a fight. But fighting is rarely the answer. Instead, try some first aid techniques to calm yourself down.

(B) Take deep breaths. Count to ten slowly. Walk away from the situation for a few minutes. Drink a glass of cold water.

(C) Your heart rate increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 분노 시 신체 반응 → 싸움 준비 신호 → 응급처치 구체 방법 순서.
det.analysis:
✅ (C)-(A)-(B): (C) 신체 반응 구체 사례(심박수↑, 얼굴, 주먹) → (A) These(=신체 반응들)는 싸움 신호 → (B) 응급처치 방법
❌ (A)-(B)-(C): These의 지칭 대상 없음
❌ (A)-(C)-(B): 순서 뒤바뀜
❌ (B)-(A)-(C): 구체 방법이 먼저 나올 수 없음
det.tip: These(A)는 (C)의 신체 반응들(심박수, 얼굴, 주먹)을 가리킨다. 지시어 추적이 핵심.

questions.passage: Anger is a natural emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated unfairly. The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a <u>destructive</u> way so that it does not control you.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 원문과 다르게 서술된 밑줄 친 부분을 바르게 고치시오.

det.korean: 분노를 '생산적인(productive)' 방식으로 관리해야 하는데, '파괴적인(destructive)'으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② destructive → productive: 원문은 a productive way
❌ ① natural은 원문 그대로
❌ ③ useful도 원문 그대로
❌ ④ unfairly도 원문 그대로
det.tip: productive(생산적인) ↔ destructive(파괴적인). 분노 관리의 핵심은 '생산적' 방식이다.

questions.passage: Take deep breaths. Count to ten slowly. Walk away from the situation for a few minutes. Drink a glass of cold water. These simple actions can help bring your body back to a calm state. Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a <u>strange</u> part of being human.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 원문과 다르게 서술된 밑줄 친 부분을 바르게 고치시오.

det.korean: 분노는 인간의 '정상적인(normal)' 부분인데, '이상한(strange)'으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ strange → normal: 원문 It is a normal part of being human.
❌ ① deep은 원문 그대로
❌ ② slowly도 원문 그대로
❌ ④ calm도 원문 그대로
det.tip: normal(정상적인) ↔ strange(이상한). 분노는 인간의 정상적인 일부이다.

questions.passage: When you feel angry, it can be helpful to ask yourself some questions. Why am I feeling this way? Is my anger ①<u>justified</u>? Am I overreacting? What is the best way to handle this situation? These questions can help you step back and think more ②<u>clearly</u> before you act. Take deep breaths. Count to ten slowly. Walk ③<u>toward</u> the situation for a few minutes. These simple actions can help bring your body back to a ④<u>calm</u> state.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 Walk away from(~에서 벗어나다)인데, toward(~를 향해)로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① justified: 정당한, 원문 일치
✅ ② clearly: 명확하게, 원문 일치
❌ ③ toward(~를 향해) → away from(~에서 벗어나): 반의어로 교체
✅ ④ calm: 차분한, 원문 일치
det.tip: away from(~에서 벗어나) ↔ toward(~를 향해). 분노 상황에서는 벗어나야 하지 다가가면 안 된다.

questions.passage: Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. Talking to someone you ①<u>trust</u>, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is problem-solving. Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on ②<u>ignoring</u> a solution to the problem that caused your anger. By understanding your anger and finding proper coping skills, you can take ③<u>control</u> of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a ④<u>healthier</u> way.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 focus on finding(찾는 데)인데, ignoring(무시하는)으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① trust: 신뢰하다, 원문 일치
❌ ② ignoring(무시하는) → finding(찾는): 해결책을 '찾는' 것이지 '무시하는' 것이 아니다
✅ ③ control: 통제, 원문 일치
✅ ④ healthier: 더 건강한, 원문 일치
det.tip: finding(찾는) ↔ ignoring(무시하는). problem-solving은 해결책을 찾는 것이다.

questions.passage: Anger is a (A)[natural / artificial] emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated (B)[unfairly / fairly]. The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a (C)[productive / destructive] way so that it does not control you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 자연스러운(natural) 감정, 부당하게(unfairly) 대우받을 때, 생산적(productive) 방식으로 관리.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ natural — unfairly — productive: 원문 일치
❌ ① artificial(인공적인): natural의 반의어
❌ ② fairly(공정하게): unfairly의 반의어
❌ ④ destructive(파괴적인): productive의 반의어
det.tip: natural ↔ artificial, unfairly ↔ fairly, productive ↔ destructive

questions.passage: Anger is a natural emotion, and <u>it</u> is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. <u>It</u> can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated unfairly.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 두 개의 it/It이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 두 it 모두 앞 문장의 주어 Anger를 가리킨다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① anger: 첫 번째 it = Anger(자연스러운 감정), 두 번째 It = anger(유용한 도구로서 알려줌)
❌ ② emotion: anger의 속성이지 it의 지칭 대상 아님
❌ ③ tool: 비유적 표현, 직접 지칭 아님
❌ ④ problem: 언급되지 않음
det.tip: 대명사 it의 선행사 추적! Anger가 주어 → it이 같은 대상을 지칭.

questions.passage: Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a normal part of being human. But you have the power to choose how you respond to your anger.
questions.stem:

Don't / let / anger / be / your / boss

questions.wa: Don't let anger be your boss
accept: Don't let anger be your boss
Don't let anger be your boss.

det.korean: 분노가 당신의 보스가 되게 하지 마라. 사역동사 let의 부정 명령문.
det.analysis:
✅ Don't let anger be your boss: Don't let(부정 명령) + anger(목적어) + be(원형부정사) + your boss(보어)
❌ Don't anger let be your boss: 어순 오류
❌ Don't let be anger your boss: 목적어 위치 오류
det.tip: Don't let + 목적어 + 동사원형: 사역동사 let의 부정 명령문.

questions.passage: Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and finding proper coping skills, you can take __________ of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a healthier way.
questions.stem:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어 한 개를 원문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

조건: '통제'라는 뜻의 명사 1개

det.korean: 감정을 통제하다(take control of). 분노의 보스가 되라는 본문 주제와 직결.
det.analysis:
✅ control: take control of = ~을 통제하다. 본문 핵심 메시지.
❌ power: '능력'이지 '통제'가 아님
❌ charge: take charge of도 가능하나 원문은 control
det.tip: take control of = ~을 통제하다. control(명사: 통제, 지배).
